items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-11-10
items.q: Earl Crumb was leader then at that point. Yeah, he was the manager... We rehearsed without a drum... I was playing fiddle up there.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah, Halloween night. And Mike Moss, he's big up there with his glass eye. I didn't know he had a glass eye. And when you look at a glass eye, it's always looking at you, you know? So I thought it was looking at me all the time. So Earl Crumb, after the night was over the next day, he says, well, the job is yours. He says, I hope you take it. I said, well, I will take it. Earl Crumb was leader then at that point. Yeah, he was the manager. He was the leader. He wasn't the leader, he was the manager. The…
And who was the bass player? Dan LeBlanc, his tuba. Well Dan was a good reader. But not that much.

items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: Earl Crumb handled all the... We told him, we'll go ahead, whatever you do is okay... that, Earl's Orchestra, none of them did either.

ctx.x: Huh? Yours was also released. Yours was released, too. Yeah. Do you have any idea how that came to be? Not the slightest idea. Was it pure coincidence, or...? Absolutely, pure coincidence. Was there any connection with a manager that...?

Not that I know of. No, no. No, Earl Crumb would have to answer that. Uh-huh. Because Earl Crumb handled all the... We told him, we'll go ahead, whatever you do is okay. And that was one orchestra that we never took a drink on the bassinet. Was that right? And, uh, we... In fact, I went through my whole career that way. Because I said, if they're paying for us... If they're paying us to play, I said, we'll have a good time. If you want a drink... I never drank. I drank more after I retired. One drink twice a…
Do you remember how you got to know about a song like Dynamite, since Henderson hadn't recorded it yet for you to hear it?
